Rory Blake: Short follow-up from today's all-hands runtime Q&A — a few quick clarifications about kernel canaries, batching defaults, and KV pinning.

Priya Desai: I'll take kernel + KV. Maya will confirm timeline.

Rory Blake: 1) Canaries: customers asked for tenant-level opt-ins in addition to per-region toggles. Is that supported?

Maya Torres: Yes. We'll support tenant opt-in + per-region toggles. Console will add a "canary channel" control (ETA June). Global default flip only after two region canaries and a 48h stability window. No silent auto-upgrades.

Ibrahim Khan: 2) Batch defaults: for new interactive endpoints should Console recommend 15ms or 40ms by default?

Priya Desai: Recommend presets: interactive -> 15ms / target_tokens=64, balanced -> 30ms / 128 tokens, throughput -> 40-50ms / 512 tokens. Adaptive batching will be opt-in initially and include p99 guardrails and a hard clamp if p99 exceeds route cap.

Rory Blake: 3) KV pinning: what's the default quota for pinned keys? Some tenants requested larger pin counts.

Priya Desai: Default pin quota is 2000 keys per tenant; customers can request an increase via Support. API example: `cache.pin=true` on session start. Pinned keys bypass soft_ttl and are only evicted under severe memory pressure.

ops-bot: Created task RUNTIME-7128 (publish canary controls + quota docs) assigned to Maya Torres.

Rory Blake: Thanks all — I'll add these bullets into the all-hands recap and link the Console mock when available. :thumbsup:
